comment: The Nintendo DS test ROMs tools/nds/build_test_roms.py builds, and how each one's verdict is read.
tools/nds/run_nds_tests.py runs them on the interpreter; tools/nds/recomp_suite.py recompiles them.
Where the expectations come from: the tests' own sources and reference pictures in the BlocksDS SDK
(github.com/blocksds/sdk, tests/, fetched to roms/nds/blocksds-tests; CC0-1.0, MIT or Zlib per file),
and roms/nds/built/VERDICTS.md, which describes how each built ROM reports. Each entry's 'source' names
its files. Text rows are quoted from the sources, or read off the test's reference picture. Nothing here
was taken from a run of this project's own machine. arm7wrestler and the window tests have no licence:
their entries hold only row counts, colours and rectangles, no text of theirs.
An entry is one run from reset: 'frames' frames with 'keys' (FRAME:BUTTONS:N, as nds_run takes them; frames
count from 0), 'keys_every' (BUTTONS held 'hold' frames, from frame 'first', every 'period' frames),
'touch' and 'lid'. Then every check must hold. 'ci_frames' is what the test's own CI waits on melonDS when
that is less than 'frames': this machine's ARM9 timing is an average and CPU-bound tests finish later.
Checks. 'console': a libnds text console read from its tilemap (32x24 cells; the character is
(entry & 0x3FF) + 32). 'rows' are exact rows without trailing spaces, 'rows_match' regular expressions for
whole rows, 'blank_elsewhere' says every other row is blank, 'stream' are regular expressions searched in
the 24 rows joined with each padded to 32 columns (text that wraps is whole there), and 'absent' are
strings that must not appear. A named group must capture the same text in every check of an entry that
uses the name. 'log': lines of the no$gba debug output of one CPU. 'picture': the SHA-256 of a rectangle
[x, y, width, height] of one screen, three bytes a pixel (the 5-bit red, green and blue), as in
tools/nds/oracle_check.py; 'reference' is the picture under roms/nds/blocksds-tests the hash was made
from. 'rects': the screen is 'background' with solid rectangles painted in order. 'colour_rows': 'rows'
bands of 'pitch' pixels from 'first_y' each hold 'pass_colour', 'fail_colour' is nowhere, no band below
holds either, and 'done_colour' is somewhere (colours are 5-bit [red, green, blue]).
'requires' names something the machine does not have (see 'requirements'); such entries are skipped
unless run with --with NAME. 'not_judged' lists the built ROMs that cannot report a verdict on a console
with only the cartridge in it, and why.

requirements.bios-exception-dispatch: the BIOS must hand undefined instructions and aborts to the program's debug handler; the replacement BIOS loops forever instead (docs/NDS-PLAN.md, The BIOS). Nintendo's BIOS does it: --with bios-exception-dispatch -- --bios9 FILE --bios7 FILE
requirements.data-cache: a model of the ARM9's data cache, which this machine does not have (docs/NDS-PLAN.md, P8)
